# Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 1 (Bi-Vb Pc1)
**ID:** Bi-Vb Pc1
**Section:** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (bi-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 1
**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on eating garlic
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-bi-vb-pc1
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul7.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Lasuṇa Sikkhāpada* ("training rule on garlic") is the first rule in the *Pācittiya* section of the *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* [SuttaCentral]. According to the origin story, the nun Thullanandā was granted permission by a lay supporter to gather garlic from his field, but took an excessive amount due to greed; her behavior drew complaints from both the field watchman and fellow nuns [Hüsken 1997]. The rule prohibits nuns from eating raw garlic under penalty of confession (*pācittiya*) [SuttaCentral]. Within its narrative framing, the text incorporates the *Suvaṇṇahaṁsa Jātaka* ("The Golden Goose Jātaka"), which is preserved in a slightly different form in the *Jātaka* collection (Ja 136) [SuttaCentral].
In the legal analysis (*padabhājaniya*) and casuistry, accepting garlic constitutes an offense of wrong conduct (*dukkaṭa*), while each bite eaten constitutes a *pācittiya* offense [Hüsken 1997]. The non-offense clause (*anāpatti*) exempts instances involving items such as onions, *bhañjanaka*, myrobalan, or *cāpa*-garlic [Hüsken 1997]. Buddhaghosa comments on this rule in the *Samantapāsādikā* [Hüsken 1997]. An English translation of the rule has been produced by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
Parallels exist across all extant Vinaya traditions: corresponding rules are preserved in the Dharmaguptaka (*Dg Bi Vb Pc 70*), Mahīśāsaka (*Mi Bi Vb Pc 70*), Sarvāstivāda (*Sarv Bi Vb Pc 72*), Mūlasarvāstivāda (*Mu Bi Vb Pc 73* in Chinese, *xct-mu-bi-vb-pc142* in Tibetan), Mahāsaṅghika (*Mg Bi Vb Pc 80*), and Mahāsaṅghika-Lokottaravāda (*san-lo-bi-vb-pc80*) traditions, as well as their respective *prātimokṣa* recensions [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects automated cross-language alignments with the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D0003-4 and related sections) and identifies extensive shared phrasing with over a hundred other Pali Vinaya texts, particularly with *Bi-Vb Pc 54*, *Bi-Vb Pc 55*, and *Bi-Vb Pc 9* [DharmaNexus].
